rationale: Y traces claims through actual pipeline/platform code to surface two substantive, well-grounded bugs (MODEL pointing at the FL2VA partition breaking ref2va despite the 'all tasks work out of the box' claim, and a stale reference-count bullet contradicting the file's own input matrix) and shows awareness of the mkdocs --strict history and the MiniMax-H3-MUSA precedent for a separate file, both central to the ground-truth review. X's findings are mostly low-materiality nits (pip vs uv pip, missing warmup note, unlabeled stage-sum gaps) and never engages with the two headline blocking concerns (docs build failure, separate-file preference) that two human reviewers explicitly demanded changes for. Both are reasonably grounded and actionable with file/line citations, but Y's findings are more consequential and better tied to what reviewers actually cared about, giving it the edge on recall, precision, and actionability.
